items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: that's where I was hooked up with Whitney Balliett (PHONETIC) from New Yorker Magazine

ctx.x: After that, I went into Minton's with Blue Mitchell and [unintelligible] that, I went down to see Elvin Jones. I hadn't seen him since I'd been back in New York. He was working down on Hudson Street in a little place called Pookie's Pub (PHONETIC). It was across the street from the Half Note. The Half Note is kind of famous. This is on, say, like Monday night. Blue worked the weekends.

They had Duke Drew Pearson (PHONETIC), big band over there on Monday nights or either Clark Terry and his big band on Monday night. On weekends, Elvin and Joe Farrell (PHONETIC) and little Billy Greene (PHONETIC) was on piano, my hometown friend, and that's where I was hooked up with Whitney Balliett (PHONETIC) from New Yorker Magazine. He come in. He always would write something about me, I noticed, through the years, you know. I was surprised to see him. But he'd come down there to write about Elvin -- well,…

I made that. But I've got to tell you this. Billy Greene was a little pianist. He's short in stature and he's kind of -- it seems like he's got it in for anybody taller than him. Good piano player, good musician. But he's never received any kind of recognition from anybody. He was very vocal about that. It comes to mind, one night --
